problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle B=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 11 & 1 & 19 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $3$rd column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 11 & 1 & 19 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & 1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & =3\cdot 1\cdot (-3)=-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(B)=-9.
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle B=\begin{bmatrix}5 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 2 & 8 \\ 9 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $3$rd column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(B) & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 1 & 2 & 8 \\ 9 & 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =2\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 6 & 0 \\ 9 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| & =2\cdot 5\cdot 6\cdot (-1)=-60.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(B)=-60.
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle E=\begin{bmatrix}\frac{7}{4} & \frac{3}{5} & 0 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 6 & -5 & -\frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{4} & \frac{2}{5} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{8}{3} & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $4$th column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $4$th column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(E) & =|\begin{aligned}\frac{7}{4} & \frac{3}{5} & 0 & \frac{1}{2} \\ 6 & -5 & -\frac{1}{4} & 0 \\ 0 & \frac{1}{4} & \frac{2}{5} & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{8}{3} & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\cdot (-1)^{1+4}|\begin{aligned}6 & -5 & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{4} & \frac{2}{5} \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}| \\  & =-\frac{1}{2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}6 & -5 & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{4} & \frac{2}{5} \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{2}\cdot |\begin{aligned}6 & -5 & -\frac{1}{4} \\ 0 & \frac{1}{4} & \frac{2}{5} \\ 0 & 0 & \frac{8}{3}\end{aligned}| & =-\frac{1}{2}\cdot (6\cdot \frac{1}{4}\cdot \frac{8}{3})=-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(E)=-2.
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix
$$
\displaystyle C=\begin{bmatrix}5 & 8 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-4 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & \,\,\,-2 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $3$rd row contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(C) & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 8 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & -4 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{3+2}|\begin{aligned}5 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $3$rd row of the $3\times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(C) & =-4\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 5 & 6 \\ 7 & 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-4)\cdot (3\cdot (-1)^{3+1}|\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}|) \\  & =-12\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & 6 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =-12(10-6) \\  & =(-12)\cdot 4 \\  & =-48.\end{aligned}
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle S=\begin{bmatrix}-3 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & -7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 3\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $4$th column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $4$th column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(S) & =|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & 2 & 0 \\ 5 & -7 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{4+4}|\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & 2 \\ 5 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & 2 \\ 5 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $3$rd column of the $3\times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(S) & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & -1 & 2 \\ 5 & -7 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot 2\cdot (-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}5 & -7 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =6\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & -7 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =6(10-0) \\  & =6\cdot 10 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle C=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 8 & -4 & 0 \\ 7 & 7 & 5 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $4$th row contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $4$th row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(C) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 5 & 0 & 0 \\ -4 & 8 & -4 & 0 \\ 7 & 7 & 5 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+1}|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & -4 & 0 \\ 7 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & -4 & 0 \\ 7 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-|\begin{aligned}5 & 0 & 0 \\ 8 & -4 & 0 \\ 7 & 5 & 3\end{aligned}| & =-1\cdot (5\cdot (-4)\cdot 3)=60.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(C)=60.
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle K=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 1 & 4 & 0 \\ -2 & \,-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 8 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $4$th column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $4$th column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(K) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 4 & 0 \\ -2 & \,-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 8 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{4+4}|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $3$rd column of the $3\times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(K) & =|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 & 4 \\ -2 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{1+3}|\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =4\cdot |\begin{aligned}-2 & -1 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(2-0) \\  & =4\cdot 2 \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle G=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 13 & 6 & 7 & -2\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $4$th column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $4$th column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(G) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 8 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 0 \\ 13 & 6 & 7 & -2\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)^{4+4}|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}(-2)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 2 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}| & =(-2)\cdot (1\cdot 2\cdot (-1))=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(G)=4.
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle H=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 10 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $3$rd row contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(H) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 & 8 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 10 & 0 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =1\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 \\ 10 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & \,\,\,-3 & 8 \\ 10 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $1$st row of the $3\times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(H) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 7 & -3 & 8 \\ 10 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot (-1)^{1+1}|\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3\cdot |\begin{aligned}-3 & 8 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}| \\  & =3(-6-0) \\  & =3\cdot (-6) \\  & =-18.\end{aligned}
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle P=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 2 \\ -3 & 0 & 8 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 & 1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $2$nd column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $2$nd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(P) & =|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 2 \\ -3 & 0 & 8 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 7 & 1\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (-1)^{4+2}|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ -3 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ -3 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

Now, notice that the $3$rd column of the $3\times 3$ determinant contains two zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P) & =-2\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 & 2 \\ -3 & 8 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-2)\cdot (2\cdot (-1)^{2+3}|\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -3 & 8\end{aligned}|) \\  & =4\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 4 \\ -3 & 8\end{aligned}| \\  & =4(8-(-12)) \\  & =4\cdot 20 \\  & =80.\end{aligned}
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle Q=\begin{bmatrix}5 & 2 & 0 & 5 \\ 2 & -4 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $4$th column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $4$th column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(Q) & =|\begin{aligned}5 & 2 & 0 & 5 \\ 2 & -4 & -4 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 3 & 0\end{aligned}| \\  & =5\cdot (-1)^{1+4}|\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-5\cdot |\begin{aligned}2 & -4 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 3\end{aligned}| & =-5\cdot (2\cdot 1\cdot 3)=-30.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(Q)=-30.
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle F=\begin{bmatrix}3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $3$rd column contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $3$rd column, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(F) & =|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & -2 \\ 4 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =(-1)\cdot (-1)^{3+3}|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =-|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}|\end{aligned}

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-|\begin{aligned}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 3 & -1 & 0 \\ 4 & 0 & -3\end{aligned}| & =-1\cdot (3\cdot (-1)\cdot (-3))=-9.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(F)=-9.
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle N=\begin{bmatrix}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{6} & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ \sqrt{3} & 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $1$st row contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(N) & =\begin{vmatrix}2 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ \sqrt{6} & -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ \sqrt{3} & 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =2\cdot (-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{vmatrix} \\  & =2\cdot \begin{vmatrix}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{vmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}2\cdot \begin{vmatrix}-1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & \sqrt{5} & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & \sqrt{5}\end{vmatrix} & =2\cdot ((-1)\cdot \sqrt{5}\cdot \sqrt{5})=-10.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(N)=-10.
$$

problem:
Find the determinant of the matrix 
$$
\displaystyle L=\begin{bmatrix}4 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 12 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ -13 & 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 9 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{bmatrix}.
$$
solution:
Notice that the $1$st row contains three zeros. So, using Laplace expansion along the $1$st row, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{det}(L) & =\begin{vmatrix}4 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 12 & 3 & 0 & 0 \\ -13 & 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 9 & 0 & 0 & -3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =4\cdot (-1)^{1+1}\begin{vmatrix}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{vmatrix} \\  & =4\cdot \begin{vmatrix}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{vmatrix}\end{aligned}
$$

The determinant of a triangular matrix is equal to the product of the entries on the main diagonal. Therefore, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}4\cdot \begin{vmatrix}3 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & -3\end{vmatrix} & =4\cdot (3\cdot (-2)\cdot (-3))=72.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we obtain

$$
det(L)=72.
$$
